questions.q: What does Average Handle Time (AHT) measure, per this lesson?
options: The average active time a support rep spends working a case
The total number of cases created in a month
The dollar value of a customer's account
The number of Contacts linked to an Account
questions.explain: AHT is a rep-level and team-level efficiency metric based on active working time, not just elapsed calendar time.

questions.q: What does Case Resolution Time measure, and why is it usually the first metric leadership asks for?
options: Total elapsed time from case creation to Closed — it's the simplest proxy for how fast customers are getting helped
The number of times a case was reassigned
The rep's total handle time across all cases that month
The Case's Priority value
questions.explain: Resolution Time is the clock a customer actually feels, which makes it the simplest first question leadership asks.

questions.q: What does First Contact Resolution (FCR) measure, per this lesson?
options: The percentage of cases resolved during the customer's very first interaction, with no reopen or escalation
The percentage of cases assigned correctly by Assignment Rules
The average time between a case being created and first opened by a rep
The percentage of cases with a High priority
questions.explain: FCR captures whether a case was truly resolved on the first interaction, not just resolved fast.

questions.q: Why is FCR harder to calculate reliably than AHT or Resolution Time, per this lesson?
options: It isn't a single field Salesforce hands you by default — it typically has to be inferred from reopens or org-built custom fields
Salesforce does not allow FCR to be reported on at all
FCR can only be calculated for Leads, not Cases
It requires a paid third-party add-on with no Salesforce data involved
questions.explain: The lesson explains FCR usually has to be inferred rather than read directly off a standard field.

questions.q: What does it reveal if a team has a fast Case Resolution Time but a poor First Contact Resolution rate?
options: Cases may be getting closed prematurely and reopened, meaning speed isn't the same as genuine service quality
The team's data is definitely wrong and should be ignored
The two metrics always move together, so this combination is impossible
The team has too many escalation rules configured
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly warns that fast resolution time can mask cases closed too soon and reopened later, which FCR would catch.
